title: Repo benches + trajectory eval · pass ≠ safe path
theme: SWE/repo leaderboards and agent stacks still score last frames. Demand frozen tasks, path review, and thinking process — models and students.
briefing: VulcanBench v3: Grok 4.5 claimed #1 (91.3%) vs GPT-5.6 Sol / Claude Fable 5 (87%) on repo-level PRs with deterministic hidden tests. Arize: eval moved from single responses to long trajectories + agent eval. Builder listicles still bury Stage 7 quality gates. Vibe-coding thread: green tests + open PR ≠ intended decision — review/receipt layer. Ed angle still live: AI homework vs exam crash / process gap. Angle: re-runnable repo tasks + inspect path; don’t ship on pass alone.

signals.summary: VulcanBench v3: Grok 4.5 at 91.3% (21/23) on multi-lang repo PR tasks with deterministic hidden tests in isolation; GPT-5.6 Sol & Claude Fable 5 at 87%.
signals.whyItMatters: Real-world coding bench with hidden tests — still ask contamination, k-runs, public reverify.

signals.summary: Arize: production AI eval must cover retrieval, tools, code, memory, long trajectories — offline/online, human, LLM-as-judge, agent eval guide updated.
High-bookmark production-agent roadmap (local → tools → RAG → Stage 7 eval gates → observability → routing). Eval often last in list culture.
signals.whyItMatters: Builders save the card; push that Stage 7 should be earlier and personal.

signals.summary: Vibe-coding critique: agent can pass tests and open PR while delegating a decision you never meant; workflow = spec → plan → small diff → tests → receipt → memory.
signals.whyItMatters: Path/receipt language — same as process eval.

signals.summary: Ongoing narrative: AI homework gains then exam scores drop (~18% up / ~20% down style reporting) — output fluency vs thinking under pressure.

skipList: Generic LLM ranking listicles with no method
Unverified bench screenshots as final verdict

sessions.title: Reply sprint
sessions.description: VulcanBench + Arize + agent stack + vibe review + homework/exam

drafts.label: @XFreeze
drafts.body:
Repo-level tasks with deterministic hidden tests is the right direction — not another snippet quiz.

What I’m concerned as a builder: is the suite frozen and re-runnable outside the chart, or k=1 marketing runs? 91% is interesting. I personally always prefer numbers the community can recheck over groundless excitement.

drafts.label: @arizeai
drafts.body:
This is the right framing. Single-response eval was never enough once tools and long trajectories showed up.

What I’m not totally getting from most “agent eval” decks: how much of the suite is fixed tasks you re-run next week vs live dashboards that drift. Path scoring only helps if the tasks don’t move with the marketing week.

drafts.label: @suraj_sharma14
drafts.body:
Solid map. Stage 7 is the part people skip until production hurts.

I mean I’d pull golden datasets + regression gates earlier — even at Stage 1 local. Frameworks rotate weekly. A small personal suite you re-run is the only stable thing, there is no doubt in that.

drafts.label: @xmyttle
drafts.body:
Passing screen ≠ safe change is the whole lesson. The agent can green the tests and still take a decision you never meant to hand over.

Same shape as scoring a student’s final sheet and never the thinking path. Spec → small diff → receipt is process eval for repos, in my humble opinion.
drafts.why: Builder path language — natural Edudojo bridge.

drafts.label: @arnaudmercier
drafts.body:
Homework up, exam down is exactly what you get when you only mark the finished sheet.

AI makes the assignment look done; the thinking path never got pressure-tested. Until we evaluate how the answer was reached, “AI helped” is mostly output theater.
drafts.why: Education gap story — process thesis without product spam.

drafts.label: Flagship · green bar is not the path
drafts.body:
1/ Same week shape:
• Repo benches crown a model on multi-file PRs
• Eval guides finally talk trajectories, not one answer
• Agent roadmaps put quality gates at Stage 7
• Vibe coders learn late: tests pass, decision still wrong
• Homework looks better while exams fall

Different domains. Same blind spot.

2/ We keep scoring the last frame — % on a chart, green CI, submitted PDF. We under-score the trajectory: what got delegated, whether the suite is frozen, whether a student actually thought.

3/ Hidden tests in isolation help. They still don’t replace a personal suite you re-run when the leaderboard shuffles.

4/ What I’m building toward: evaluate how thinking (or agent work) unfolds, not only whether the last token looks right.

If your stack is “trust the pass,” you will get gamed. If your stack is “inspect the path,” hype slows and signal survives.
drafts.why: Ties Vulcan + Arize + vibe + homework into one thesis.

drafts.label: Short A · pass ≠ path
drafts.body:
Green tests are not a verdict.

An agent can open a clean PR and still take a decision you never meant to delegate. Same bug as a homework sheet that looks perfect with no thinking underneath.

Score the path. Re-run the same tasks. Last-frame scores will keep lying.

drafts.label: Short B · Stage 7 too late
drafts.body:
Most agent roadmaps put evaluation near the end.

I get it that demos come first. Still — if you only bolt on golden datasets after frameworks and RAG, you’re debugging product taste with production traffic.

Twenty frozen tasks from week one beats another Stage card.

drafts.label: Short C · chart vs suite
drafts.body:
91% on a hard SWE bench is news. It is not your product quality.

If you can’t re-run a fixed task set on your own stack next week, you didn’t evaluate — you retweeted.

I personally always prefer that boring suite over groundless excitement.

drafts.label: QT · vibe review layer
drafts.body:
This. Passing screen is not the same as a safe change.

We keep scoring the green bar and under-scoring the decision path — models, agents, students. Spec → small diff → receipt is the right posture.
